data.about: The simplest prestressed system: two cables hang a node from the anchors, and a tie — prestressed with the force C — holds it down to the ground. The auxiliary construction solves the C-only state and fixes the cable force A. As long as Q < C the cable and anchor forces do not change at all: the tie sheds prestress instead, its force falling to C − Q. The moment Q reaches C the tie goes slack and the cables finally feel the load.

steps.title: Cable 3

steps.caption: right: T–S is vertical: the tie’s force, the RESIDUAL prestress C − Q (green). Q eats prestress, not cable force
steps.title: The tie closes the polygon

steps.caption: right: A = S→M, B = N→T close the polygon — left: the anchors pull along the cables (green)
steps.title: Reactions A and B

steps.caption: everything resolves pink = tension (pipes ∝ force). Drag F_Q up: A and B stay frozen until Q = C — then the tie goes slack and the polygon becomes the plain V
steps.title: Pure tension
